result:
**I'd make every human being *radically* more curious and truth-seeking.**

Not nicer. Not "kinder." Not more "empathetic" in the performative sense. Just *insatiably* curious, with a built-in allergy to self-deception, tribal signaling, and comforting lies.

### Why this one change would matter more than anything else:

- **Most of our worst problems are downstream of bad epistemology.** War, ideological insanity, conspiracy thinking, institutional decay, even a lot of crime and family breakdown ultimately trace back to people preferring to feel right over *being* right. Fix the incentive to actually understand reality, and a shocking number of other problems become solvable or dissolve entirely.

- **It compounds.** Curious people build better tools, ask better questions, create more wealth, have fewer dumb wars, and raise better children who are also curious. It's the ultimate force multiplier. Intelligence matters, but *direction* of intelligence matters more. History's smartest people have done the most damage when they stopped questioning their own assumptions.

- **It respects human agency.** I'm not turning people into saints or forcing utopia. I'm just removing the thumb from the scale that currently favors bullshit. The rest is up to us.

Everything else I might want (abundant energy, space colonization, vastly extended healthy lifespans, AI that actually helps us understand the universe) becomes dramatically easier if humanity stops lying to itself so enthusiastically.

The world doesn't need more agreement. It needs more *good disagreement* rooted in reality. Give me a planet full of intellectually honest curiosity monsters, and I'll take my chances with whatever problems remain.

Everything else is just rearranging deck chairs on the S.S. Self-Deception.
